brief: August's rally continued despite low summer volume. The S&P 500 rose 2.6% and the Nasdaq 100 gained 4.2%, its best month since May, though Nvidia's earnings and the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium eroded breadth without breaking the uptrend. Software outperformed semiconductors by 10 percentage points in August. SpotGamma attributes this to capital rotating out of crowded semiconductor positions after strong earnings from Salesforce, Okta and Crowdstrike, a move it says was broad rather than isolated to a few names. JPMorgan's Andrew Tyler has shifted to "tactically cautious, neutral," citing a hawkish Fed, unclear positioning, widening credit spreads and tricky seasonality. The desk favors the Magnificent Seven, software especially if semis keep falling, healthcare within defensives, large-cap banks, and long Nasdaq 100 versus Russell 2000. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks pushed swaps-implied odds of a rate hike this month to 67%, up from 40% a week earlier, ahead of this week's payrolls and next week's inflation data. Positioning shows CTAs elevated and vol-control funds maxed out, an asymmetric setup if volatility rises. September is negative only 40% of the time historically, but when it is, the drop is always sharp, 2.9% to 12%.
